I will keep my land in the usual `winter wheat + summer maize` rotation. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is the crop pattern I know best and trust most. At my age, with only primary schooling, I would not gamble on a complicated cash crop that needs tighter market timing or more technical management. Wheat and maize are easier for me to manage, the inputs and machine work are familiar, and the sales are straightforward.

For the winter season, I will grow winter wheat on all my land. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want more even emergence and steadier yield. I will do rotary tillage before sowing, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate a few key times, and keep pesticide spraying limited to what is necessary for weeds, aphids, and disease. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away on the same land. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives the best yield here. I will keep tillage light and mostly no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and moisture, then manage fertilizer, irrigation, and pests in a simple, practical way. My goal is not the highest possible yield; my goal is a stable harvest with work I can handle myself and costs I can control.
